factProposals.value: Work orders read assets from GIS (getAsset) and write each work order's title, type, priority, status and update time back onto the selected assets (linkWorkOrder). Currently against a stand-in GIS, not the city's GIS.
Selecting a GIS asset autofills the work order's work type, address and coordinates, and stores a snapshot of the asset's type, name and attributes on the work order.
Work order, work_order_assets, gis_sync and append-only audit_entries tables exist in SQLite; every create, update and complete writes an audit entry with actor, time and before/after values.
A work order cannot be completed without a completion note, and a completed work order can no longer be updated or completed again.
The city GIS product, its URL, credentials and asset schema are not known yet; the stand-in assets and their fields are assumptions.

decisions.statement: Use Node.js with its built-in SQLite and test runner, with no external packages.
decisions.rationale: Nothing to install; runs locally; one language with the Command Center. The database is reached only through server/db.js so it can move to Postgres later.

decisions.statement: Verify GIS behaviour against a stand-in GIS behind a client interface rather than the city's GIS.
decisions.rationale: No access or credentials to the city GIS; the student approved the stand-in.

decisions.statement: Save each change and its audit entry in one transaction, and roll the change back if the audit write fails.
decisions.rationale: The SAFE requirement and the Trust criterion: no work order action may exist without its audit record.

decisions.statement: Push changes to GIS after the database commit through a queued gis_sync row, with timeout and capped retries, instead of inside the transaction.
decisions.rationale: A slow or failed GIS call must not lose or block the work order; failed pushes stay retryable.

decisions.statement: Make create idempotent through an optional caller-supplied request_id.
decisions.rationale: A double-click or network retry must not create two work orders.

limitations.statement: The stand-in GIS keeps writes in memory only; nothing is persisted to a GIS database.
When a failed GIS push later succeeds, its error message is cleared; the gis_sync row keeps only the attempt count, not a full history of each try.
Retrying failed GIS pushes is a function call (syncPending); nothing runs it automatically yet.
There is no HTTP API or user interface yet; work orders are created through module functions, tests and the demo script.
Node's built-in SQLite module is marked experimental in Node 22.
